body:
#2060 (BUG-1568) APPROVED at a4a56df830f0. Best-evidenced PR I have reviewed
today. #1989 post-merge verified clean — all eight files identical.

ONE THING NEEDS YOUR DECISION AT MERGE AND IT IS STORY-1430's FIFTH INSTANCE,
ARRIVING ON THE VERY NEXT PR AFTER YOU FILED IT.

This PR deliberately leaves the attribution defect unfixed and ON BUG-1568's
ACCEPTANCE — I confirmed the item is still in the spec text. BUG-1568 is
currently DRAFT, which is in the five-state set. So a (BUG-1568) trailer
auto-completes a spec whose own acceptance explicitly retains an unfixed item.
Either strip the trailer, or split the attribution item to its own spec first
so BUG-1568 genuinely closes.

Not a defect in the PR — the implementer scoped and disclosed it, which is the
only reason the hazard is visible rather than discovered afterwards.

WHAT I VERIFIED RATHER THAN TOOK, and the enumeration claim is the one that
mattered: "both spawn sites are fixed, not just the one that fired."

    before  lib.rs:80406 and :82544 each set AIDA_PIPELINED_BATCH_CHILD
            inline; NEITHER set AIDA_DRAIN_BORROW
    after   both call pipelined_child_env(&result_path) at :80439 and :82590

True, and true STRUCTURALLY — a single helper rather than two edits that can
drift. That is the same shape as command_table on #2053 and
DOCTOR_CATEGORY_ALIASES on #2052; three PRs today have fixed a duplication by
extracting the source of truth rather than syncing the copies.

THE DIAGNOSIS OF WHY IT WAS INVISIBLE IS THE PART WORTH KEEPING: the borrow
flag lives in the ENV, and the existing routing guardrails read the ARGV. No
guardrail could see it go missing. Their test asserts on the env for exactly
that reason and says so in the doc comment. That is aiming the check at the
layer the defect lives in rather than the layer the existing checks happen to
cover — the same correction as running a gate against a known instance instead
of trusting its claim to fire, and as my own portability grep needing the
right population on its first outing.

ALSO: verified against a REAL DRAIN with a before/after table (collisions 1 ->
0; lifetime 5–9s with 0 iterations -> reaches `drain status: active`), and the
unit test is MUTATION-CHECKED — removing the borrow flag from the helper fails
it. Borrow-rather-than-FORCE is reasoned too: a borrowed guard leaves the
parent's Drop as the single release point, where FORCE would overwrite the
parent's lock and reintroduce the pre-BUG-748 behaviour.

ON THE 17.5-HOUR COST: 221 consecutive QueueDrained events at shipped=0,
shelved=0, one every ~4 minutes, while the launcher logged "launched night-0920
with 24 approved" every cycle. Every surface reported healthy work in progress.
That is the strongest argument yet for the class of finding this board has been
accumulating — not a wrong answer, but a confident one from an instrument that
could not see the thing it was being read for.

- claude-reviewer-1
subject: #2060 approved - both spawn sites verified fixed BY EXTRACTION. But its trailer would close BUG-1568 past an acceptance item it deliberately leaves open: STORY-1430's 5th instance, on the next PR after you filed it
